data.name: Niddat
data.gender_notes: Niddat is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Made of soft, thin, and delicate materials. The name Niddat carries the meaning “Delicate” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Niddat usually hope their child will grow to embody delicate and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a gentle soul with a soft heart, one who is easily moved by emotions and is sensitive to the feelings of others.
data.etymology: Niddat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Delicate.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Niddat total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Niddat" in Islamic culture symbolizes beauty, tenderness, and elegance. It is a name given to a girl, evoking images of delicate flowers or soft cloth, making it an exquisite and cherished name in Islamic communities.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual sense, the name "Niddat" can be seen as a reminder of the inherent softness and gentleness that is present within every soul, regardless of whether the person is a man or a woman. It encourages individuals to strive towards being kind, compassionate, and gentle towards themselves and others, while maintaining a sense of strength and resilience in their actions and beliefs. Additionally, the name represents the concept of the created world being a manifestation of Allah's divine wisdom and mercy, with all its delicate and intricate details reflecting the beauty and tenderness of the Creator.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Delicate" symbolizes Made of soft, thin, and delicate materials. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Niddat serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of delicate.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami, in his book 'al-Fatawa al-Hadithah fi al-Masajid wa al-Jamia'at', mentions a person named Niddat al-Hanafi.
historical_references.context: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami was a prominent Islamic scholar and jurist. He mentions a person named Niddat al-Hanafi in his book, indicating that this person was a Hanafi scholar or jurist during the 16th century.
